candidates.name: Mutekiya
candidates.why: Ikebukuro's best-known tonkotsu-shoyu ramen, rich soup and thick chashu, and it stays open until 4am, which makes it the default after-drinks bowl near Ninja House. 2026 Google reviews put the queue at 10 to 30 minutes and say about half the customers are foreign. Good, not life-changing, but the late hours earn it a slot.
candidates.best_time: Late night after drinks (after 23:00) or a weekday mid-afternoon; Saturday 18:00 queues reach about 30 min
candidates.price: about ¥1,000–1,500 pp (honmaru ¥1,150; toppings like garlic cost extra)
candidates.group_of_8: Counter only: queue together, eat in 2–3 waves; turnover is fast
candidates.hours: Daily 10:30–04:00 (Google). Year-end: closed 31 Dec–3 Jan per HotPepper, so it is open for the 15–19 Dec stay and 26–29 Dec

evidence.note: 4.2 from about 8,300 reviews; Oct 2026 reviews: 4 people ahead on a weekday 13:30, 30 min on a Saturday at 18:00; counter only; many foreign customers

candidates.name: Kinsuien
candidates.why: Wagyu all-you-can-eat yakiniku, plus seafood (crab), offal, cold noodles and soup, about 3 minutes from Ikebukuro East exit. Courses come with all-you-can-drink, which suits a group that loves to drink and is counting yen. 2026 reviews in Japanese and Chinese are consistently strong. Many reviews are recent and from Chinese visitors, so treat the rating with some caution.
candidates.best_time: Dinner from 17:00; a good first-night or second-night group dinner from Ninja House
candidates.price: Wagyu AYCE courses about ¥4,300–7,600 pp; reviewers cite ¥4,290, ¥6,900 and ¥7,590 courses; all-you-can-drink add-on or bundled
candidates.booking: Book via HotPepper (linked from its Google listing) a week or two ahead for 8; entry limited when busy
candidates.group_of_8: Book a table for 8 ahead; restaurant caps entry at peak times

candidates.why: The budget yakiniku all-you-can-eat by Ikebukuro East exit, from about ¥2,000. It is the cheap fallback if Kinsuien is full or the group wants to save yen for drinks. Open until midnight every day.

candidates.price: AYCE from about ¥2,000 pp (HotPepper listing); about ¥2,500 (120 RMB) per Xiaohongshu

candidates.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
candidates.why: Still the best seafood breakfast crawl in Tokyo: tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, tuna, kaisen-don and oysters from about 460 shops. Graze on street food rather than queue for one famous kaisen-don shop. The end of December is the market's busiest time of year, so go early.
candidates.best_time: 07:30–10:00. Avoid Sun 27 Dec, when the wholesale market and many shops are shut. Best on Thu 17 or Fri 18 Dec, or early Mon 28 Dec, when year-end crowds are already building
candidates.dates: Year-end shopping crowds build from about 27 Dec and peak 28–30 Dec; many shops close on market holidays (Sundays, holidays, some Wednesdays)
candidates.group_of_8: Street food is easy for 8; sit-down kaisen-don shops seat small groups, so split up
candidates.hours: Main retail 9:00–14:00 (trade buying 6:00–9:00); many shops shut from about 14:00

candidates.name: Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai
candidates.why: The Edo-style food street that opened in 2024 beside Toyosu fish market: seafood bowls, grilled skewers and a food court under one roof, plus a 24-hour onsen building. It is calmer and easier for 8 than Tsukiji, and pairs with teamLab Planets next door.
candidates.best_time: Lunch, or combine with a teamLab Planets slot
candidates.hours: Food building 10:00–22:00, open all year (GO TOKYO); hot-spring building 24 h. Shop hours vary by season; year-end hours not published

candidates.name: Tsukishima Monja Moheji (main shop)
candidates.name_ja: 月島もんじゃ もへじ 総本店
candidates.why: Monjayaki is the Tokyo-only dish, and Tsukishima's Monja Street is where to eat it: a gooey griddle mess you cook together at the table with beer. It is the best group-of-8 meal in Tokyo. Moheji ranked first in Tsukishima for foreign visitors in 2025, and staff help first-timers. Kondo (founded 1950) is the old-school alternative.
candidates.best_time: Dinner; book or arrive before 18:00. Pairs with Toyosu or Tsukiji the same day (one stop on the Oedo line)
candidates.booking: Reserve ahead for 8 (Moheji has several branches incl. hanare nearby; Kondo recommends booking)
candidates.group_of_8: Two adjacent griddle tables of 4 is standard; a 9-person group visit is documented
candidates.hours: Daily about 10:30–23:00 (Google). Year-end: Kondo closes 31 Dec–3 Jan; Moheji year-end hours not found

candidates.name: Ameyoko
candidates.why: Ueno's old black-market street, at its loudest at year-end, when stalls sell tuna, crab, roe and New Year food. Cheap kaisen-don, skewers, fruit sticks and standing beers line the way. The 26–29 Dec stay lands in the year-end market, so it is a sight in itself. Bar-alley drinking here belongs to the night list; this entry is for grazing.
candidates.best_time: Morning to early afternoon on 26–28 Dec; avoid 30–31 Dec, when it is shoulder to shoulder
candidates.dates: Year-end market crowds 27–31 Dec, peaking 30–31 Dec

candidates.name: Fuunji
candidates.why: Tokyo's benchmark tsukemen: thick noodles dipped in a dense chicken-and-fish broth, about 6 minutes' walk from Shinjuku South exit. One of the few famous Shinjuku ramen shops that is worth the queue, rather than a tourist line.
candidates.best_time: Be there by 10:40 for the 11:00 opening, or about 16:45 for the 17:00 dinner opening. By 11:15 the queue was already past 50 people (end-2025 review). Go on Sat 26 or Mon 28 Dec, not Sun 27

notes: Tokyo · food: Area logic. Stay 1 (15–19 Dec, Ninja House, Toshima): Ikebukuro East exit is the food base; Mutekiya (to 4am) and Kinsuien/Mugendo AYCE yakiniku are all within about 5 min of each other. The first-night dinner after the Haneda 15:00 landing is easy there (Keikyu + Yamanote/Marunouchi to Ikebukuro, about 60–70 min). Do Tsukiji (breakfast) + Tsukishima monja (dinner) + Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai/teamLab as one east-side day: all on the Oedo/Yurikamome lines. Best on Thu 17 or Fri 18 Dec; Wed 16 may be a market holiday. Stay 2 (26–29 Dec, Garfield House, Shinjuku): breakfast at Shinpachi Shokudo (7:00), Fuunji tsukemen at opening, Tsunahachi tempura (book TableCheck), Uobei and Isomaru 24h for late nights. Ameyoko is on the Yamanote from Shinjuku/Ikebukuro: go 26–28 Dec mornings, avoid 30–31. Year-end traps: Sun 27 Dec, the Tsukiji market and many shops are shut; independent shops (Fuunji, Kondo monja) take year-end breaks from about 29–31 Dec; Mutekiya and Kondo close 31 Dec–3 Jan (after the trip). Chains (Isomaru, Uobei, Shinpachi) are the safe bets on 28–29 Dec. Budget: AYCE yakiniku with drinks (¥2,000–7,600) and monja are the best-value group feasts; book Kinsuien, Moheji and Tsunahachi for 8 two to three weeks ahead. Departure 29 Dec: eat at Haneda T3 Edo Koji before security, since 29 Dec is a peak travel day.
